label: Highest Peaks
intro: The world's great summits, ranked by elevation above sea level. Measurements are rounded to the nearest metre.

items.title: Mount Everest
items.detail: Nepal / China (Tibet). Official height of 8,848.86 m was jointly announced by Nepal and China in December 2020.

items.title: K2 (Chogori)
items.detail: Pakistan / China. The second-highest mountain and widely considered the most demanding of the 8,000ers.

items.title: Kangchenjunga
items.detail: India / Nepal. The third-highest peak, first climbed by Joe Brown and George Band.

items.title: Aconcagua
items.detail: Argentina. Highest peak outside Asia and the highest in both the Southern and Western Hemispheres.

items.title: Denali
items.detail: USA (Alaska). The highest peak in North America, with one of the greatest vertical rises of any mountain on Earth.

items.title: Kilimanjaro
items.detail: Tanzania. The world's tallest free-standing mountain and Africa's highest summit.

items.title: Broad Peak
items.detail: Pakistan. The 12th-highest peak and the only 8,000er with three summits, nicknamed 'the mountain of a thousand roads'.

items.title: Mount Vinson
items.detail: Antarctica. The highest mountain on the continent, a long way from any support.

label: First Ascents
intro: The moments when humanity first stood on top of the world's most coveted summits.

items.title: Mont Blanc
items.detail: Jacques Balmat and Michel-Gabriel Paccard make the first ascent, launching modern alpinism.

items.title: Annapurna I
items.detail: First 8,000-metre peak to be climbed, by Maurice Herzog and Louis Lachenal.

items.title: Mount Everest
items.detail: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reach the summit on 29 May.

items.title: K2
items.detail: Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni, Italian expedition led by Ardito Desio.

items.title: K2 in winter
items.detail: Ten Nepali climbers stand on the summit on 16 January: the last 8,000er climbed in winter.

items.title: All fourteen 8,000ers
items.detail: Reinhold Messner completes the set with Lhotse on 16 October.

items.title: Gasherbrum I
items.detail: Peter Schoening climbs to the summit alone on 6 July after injuries to the rest of the summit party.

items.title: The Eiger north face
items.detail: Toni Kurz's death in 1932 defines the route's reputation; the first ascent comes six years later.

label: Fastest & Most
intro: Feats of endurance, efficiency and sheer persistence.

items.title: Matterhorn North Face
items.detail: Dani Arnold's 2015 speed record: 1 hour 46 minutes from the start of the route to the summit.

items.title: All fourteen 8,000ers
items.detail: Nirmal Purja's 'Project Possible' in 2019 shattered the previous record of just under eight years.

items.title: Everest without oxygen or fixed ropes
items.detail: Kilian Jornet's 2017 ascent from Rongbuk Monastery, the pinnacle of fast-and-light mountaineering.

items.title: Most Everest summits
items.detail: Kami Rita Sherpa of Nepal holds the record for the most ascents of Everest by anyone.

items.title: Fastest ascent of K2
items.detail: The standard K2 route has been climbed in under two days by pre-supported teams moving with fixed caches.

items.title: Hour for the world's biggest walls
items.detail: On a big-wall push, elite alpinists climb and sleep a full day at altitude, every day, for weeks.

label: Youngest & Oldest
intro: Everest does not care how old you are, but extraordinary people have stood on top at both ends of life.

items.title: Youngest on Everest
items.detail: Jordan Romero of the USA summited from the Tibetan side aged 13 years and 10 months. Both Nepal and China have since raised minimum ages.

items.title: Oldest on Everest
items.detail: Japanese mountaineer Yuichiro Miura reached the summit aged 80 years and 224 days, after three heart operations.

items.title: Youngest to climb all fourteen 8,000ers
items.detail: Nepal's Nima Rinji Sherpa completed the full set while still a teenager, a generation after Messner first did it.

label: Women's Records
intro: Pioneers who redefined what was possible, and who the mountains were open to.

items.title: First woman on Everest
items.detail: Junko Tabei of Japan reaches the summit on 16 May 1975.

items.title: First woman on K2
items.detail: Wanda Rutkiewicz of Poland, who also became the first European woman on Everest in 1978.

items.title: All 14 without bottled oxygen
items.detail: Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner of Austria is the first woman to climb all fourteen 8,000ers without supplemental oxygen.

items.title: Most Everest summits by a woman
items.detail: Lhakpa Sherpa of Nepal, who reached the summit for the tenth time in 2022.

items.title: First woman on the Eiger north face
items.detail: Evelyn Camissac of Switzerland became the first woman to climb the north face, five years before it was first climbed without a fixed rope.

items.title: Seven Summits in a single year
items.detail: Chantal Mauduit finished all seven continental summits within one calendar year, topping out on Aconcagua in December.
